title: Al-Akhir, the Last
tomorrow: how can one verse call God both the Outward and the Inward?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Al-Awwal, the First, and bismillah at every beginning. The line: first. Same verse, next Name. If He's there before the first thing, who's there after the last?

Nobody posts their hands after a double shift. In Medina, Fatima, the daughter of the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, has hands worn raw from turning the stone mill. She hears her father has received captives who could work in a household, so she goes to ask him for help. He isn't home. She leaves word with Aisha and goes back. That night, after she and her husband Ali have lain down to sleep, someone comes to the door. It's him.
screen: `HANDS RAW FROM THE MILL.` → `SHE ASKS FOR HELP.` → `A KNOCK AT BEDTIME.`

segments.voice: They start to get up. He tells them to stay where they are and sits down between them; Ali remembers the coolness of his feet. Then, as Sahih al-Bukhari tells it, he asks: shall I not teach you something better than what you asked for? When you go to bed, say Allahu akbar thirty-four times, subhanallah thirty-three times, alhamdulillah thirty-three times. That, he says, is better for you than a servant. It's a hard answer to hear, and the hadith doesn't pretend otherwise. She asked for help with her hands, and he gave her words for the end of the day. It doesn't say her hands stopped hurting. It says what she was given. Why bedtime? Today's Name helps. Al-Akhir, the Last, from the same verse as yesterday's: "He is the First and the Last." A du'a the Prophet taught for lying down, in Sahih Muslim, says: You are the Last, and there is nothing after You. So the day's last words go to the Last. And one detail to tell a friend tonight: in another report, Ali says he never once dropped those bedtime words after that night.
screen: `STAY WHERE YOU ARE.` · `SOMETHING BETTER THAN A SERVANT.` · `NOTHING AFTER YOU.` · `THE DAY'S LAST WORDS.` · then, large: `LAST.`

segments.voice: Count slowly on your fingers: subhanallah, glory be to God; alhamdulillah, praise be to God; Allahu akbar, God is greatest. Don't race for the number. Go as far as the sit allows, as if these were the last words of your day.
Al-Akhir. The Last, after everything, with nothing after Him: the Name that gets the day's final words.
Pocket this one: last, the One who stays when the lights go off. Sleep well when it's time.
